parts.note: the stock opening words of a fairy tale told to children

explanation.surface: Someone recalls how a first schoolyard crush got started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' suggests a love affair, but here it is a fairy story, and its 'beginning' is the traditional opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales customarily open with this formula, so it is literally the start of a story for children.

explanation.surface: Someone notes the characters who appear in the Hebrew scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures are digits or quantities; the fourth book of the Hebrew Bible also bears this title.

parts.note: the Greek god of love strikes people with arrows so they give their hearts away

explanation.surface: A villain whose prey become discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose heart' seems to mean despair; here it means falling in love, the work of the god of desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek love god's arrows make people fall in love, surrendering their affections.

clue.text: Go ahead and get caught in deeper trouble

indicators.note: the cricket abbreviation sits inside the scrambled letters of deeper
deeper in trouble is taken as the word deeper being disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone moves on and only lands in a worse fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' scrambles DEEPER to PREEDE, and 'in' puts C (caught) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To come before something in time or order is to go ahead of it.

parts.note: table linen is rolled up and slipped into holders at a formal dinner

explanation.surface: Something gets rolled through hoops, like a circus trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The rings are serviette rings on a dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviettes are often rolled and pushed through decorative holders at a laid table.

parts.note: a sharp spike of a fork, used to spear food and lift it

explanation.surface: A place where passengers are collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking-up point' sounds like a bus stop; it is a literal point that picks food up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fork's prong is a pointed spike that spears and lifts food.

explanation.surface: A lookout keeps an eye open aboard a naval vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over is to keep under observation; a nineteenth-century class of low armoured gunship bore this name.

parts.note: the deep is the sea, so a scientist who studies it

explanation.surface: A scholar absorbed in profound thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep study' suggests concentration; 'the deep' is the sea, and this person studies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine scientist studies the sea, known poetically as the deep.

clue.text: His aim is to see that people settle

definitions.text: His aim is to see that people settle

parts.words: His aim is to see that people settle
parts.note: settle means pay what they owe, not move into a home

explanation.surface: Someone working to get people to put down roots in a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' suggests making a home; here it means settling accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff-like agent recovers unpaid money, making people clear their accounts.

explanation.surface: Someone resolves a match result, or pays off an old grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle oneself is to calm down, and to score is to write music.

clue.text: For punishment, keep in and cane, perhaps

parts.note: to pen is to keep in an enclosure

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of cane may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A teacher threatens detention and a caning as discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures school discipline; 'For' is only a link before the definition, and 'perhaps' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of self-punishment is undertaken to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: A word of approval for those in favour

parts.note: saying yes is a word that approves

explanation.surface: Someone expresses approval for the supporters of a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary vote the supporters of a motion are counted as this group.

clue.text: Cat in middle of well is in awkward position

indicators.note: the central letters of well sit inside the word for a tight spot

parts.note: being in a fix is being in an awkward position

indicators.note: the centre letters of the word well are taken

explanation.surface: A cat stuck halfway down a well, in a real predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is the definition: Felix is a well-known cartoon cat. 'is in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix is a famous cartoon feline and a common name for pet cats.

parts.note: a proofreader's instruction to let the marked text stand unchanged

explanation.surface: A regular bank payment set up by a print shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'standing order' sounds like a bank arrangement; it is literally an order to let words stand.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin proof-correction mark tells the typesetter to ignore a deletion and keep the original.

explanation.surface: Railway services, one or a couple of them.
explanation.walkthrough: A dental brace trains teeth into line; a brace of birds is two. 'one or' joins the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodontic supports straighten teeth by steady pressure, and a pair of game birds is counted as this.

explanation.surface: Someone tosses provisions into a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: In the American West, the chuck wagon carried the cowboys' food, called chuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something is to throw it, and cowboy slang for grub gave its name to the cook wagon.

explanation.surface: Someone follows the instructions on a posted sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule is to obey it, and to spot something is to see it.

clue.text: Half the school get zero, unusual for music

indicators.note: the first half of the six letters of school is taken
unusual means the letters of zero appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Half the pupils score nothing, which is rare for a music exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes SCH from SCHOOL; 'unusual' turns ZERO into ERZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively movement in a symphony or sonata is a piece of music of this kind.

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rescued are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Agreements were saved after collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a noun for agreements; it is the verb meaning shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that contracts gets smaller, that is, it lessens.

explanation.surface: A marksman is posted up among a ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert marksman is called this, and it is also a round wooden block with holes used to tighten a ship's shrouds.

clue.text: Sausage and veal cooked in sauce

indicators.note: the cooked letters are placed inside the name of the sauce

parts.note: soy is a salty sauce

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of veal are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe for a sausage made with veal and simmered in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a seasoned smoked sausage sold in British chip shops. 'cooked' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy red-skinned British sausage is a chip-shop staple.

clue.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

definitions.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

indicators.note: the exclamation is put inside the rearranged pub word
perhaps signals the letters of local are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a drink is sold and answers: at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The local' is British slang for a nearby pub. 'perhaps' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; the whole clue also describes what a pub sells.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer, wine and spirits are what a pub sells, all intoxicating drink.

clue.text: Man devoured by lion, perhaps-a circus performer

indicators.note: the man's name is swallowed inside the big animal

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is eaten by a lion during a circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a man's name here; 'devoured by' signals the container, with the A of 'perhaps-a' as the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or trapeze artist performs gymnastic feats under the big top.

clue.text: Essex port which is set around a river

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of which go around the other pieces
set means the letters of which are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A guide to a harbour town built along a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: HARWICH is a ferry port in Essex, a county east of London. 'is set' turns WHICH into HWICH, and 'around' wraps it round A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Essex coast is a ferry harbour for crossings to the Netherlands.

clue.text: Give us a song at the piano!

definitions.text: Give us a song at the piano!

parts.words: Give us a song at the piano!
parts.note: a request to perform music on the keyboard, one word of command

explanation.surface: Party guests urge someone to sing a tune at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is an imperative asking someone to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform on a keyboard instrument is to make music on it.

clue.text: Declares a piece of poetry lacks point

indicators.note: lacks means the compass letter is taken out of the poetry word

parts.note: a verse is a piece of poetry
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A critic says a poem has no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like 'purpose'; it is a compass point, E, which 'lacks' removes from VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something firmly is to affirm or assert it.

clue.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

definitions.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

parts.words: If there's a man around, he's from the US
parts.note: put the letters of a man around the name sought and the result is a citizen of the US

explanation.surface: Any man found nearby must be an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally: A MAN placed around this name spells AMERICAN, someone from the US.
explanation.definitionFit: This common boy's name fits inside a man to make a word for a US national.

explanation.surface: Someone protests against excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims or goals are purposes, and tips or limits are the farthest points.

parts.note: fair means pale-skinned, not honourable: these were Zulu warriors

explanation.surface: Combatants who cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' suggests honest play; it means light-skinned, and these were Zulu regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu army regiments were dark-skinned warriors, so not fair in complexion.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit about the compass letter
possibly signals another possible arrangement of learnt

explanation.surface: Someone may have studied Eastern ideas about everlasting life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns LEARNT into ETRNAL, and 'about' wraps it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting never dies or ends.

clue.text: Young Italian graduate doctor in love

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A young doctor fresh from university falls in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a little child or baby boy.

parts.note: an old weather rhyme about a glowing evening sky being the shepherd's delight

explanation.surface: Angels appear to shepherds in the Nativity story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nativity is a decoy: the old rhyme runs 'Red sky at night, shepherd's delight', promising fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The weather proverb says a glowing evening sky pleases those who tend sheep.
